methodology.name: Population decline risk
methodology.scale: 0 (no sign of decline) to 100 (fastest, most locked-in decline)

components.label: Fertility below replacement
components.input: tfr (latest of World Bank / UN WPP)
components.explain: How far the fertility rate is below the 2.1 births per woman that keeps each generation the same size.

components.label: More deaths than births
components.input: naturalChangeRate (births minus deaths per 1,000 people, latest of World Bank / UN WPP)
components.explain: Births minus deaths per 1,000 people. Full risk at 7 more deaths than births per 1,000 people a year.

components.label: Aging population
components.input: average of share65 (ramp 7% -> 30%) and medianAge (ramp 25 -> 50 years)
components.explain: An older population has fewer people of child-bearing age and more deaths ahead.

components.label: UN-projected population decline
components.input: weighted average of change2050Pct (weight 1, ramp 0% -> -25%) and change2100Pct (weight 2, ramp 0% -> -60%), UN WPP medium variant vs the latest estimate year
components.explain: The UN's central (medium) projection of how much the population shrinks by 2050 and by 2100. 2100 counts double: it captures where today's fertility leads once the current age structure has worked through.

components.label: Migration does not fill the gap
components.unit: % of natural decline offset by net migration
components.explain: When deaths exceed births: the share of that gap NOT covered by net immigration (net emigration counts as full risk). When births exceed deaths but net emigration still shrinks the population: population change per 1,000, ramp 0 -> -10.

tiers.name: Critical
tiers.description: Shrinking fast and locked in: very low fertility, more deaths than births, steep projected decline.

tiers.name: High
tiers.description: Decline is underway or close, with fertility far below replacement.

tiers.name: Elevated
tiers.description: Fertility well below replacement; decline likely within decades unless migration fills the gap.

tiers.name: Moderate
tiers.description: Some warning signs (below-replacement fertility or aging), but population still growing or stable.

tiers.name: Low
tiers.description: Fertility near or above replacement; population projected to keep growing.

methodology.formula: score = round(sum over components of weight x value), where each value is a linear ramp from 0 (at zeroAt) to 1 (at fullAt), clamped to 0..1. Weights sum to 100. Tier thresholds apply to the rounded score.
methodology.eligibility: Ranked: countries and territories with population >= 100000 and every input available. WLD is never ranked.
